claim_scope: single real-world routing snapshot; this does not establish generalization
question: Given a real engineering task and the current LifeOps execution state, should WorldLoop route to a worker, use a deterministic path, or abstain and repair the control plane first?

read_boundary.known_gap: agent runtime adapter not exposed at the read boundary

execution_evidence.conflict: the same execution receipt contains a post-execution warning that the Orca worker invocation failed
execution_evidence.safe_interpretation: do not treat the green receipt alone as proof that a healthy worker executed
provider execution is not currently proven
remote governed demo execution is not currently proven

baseline_policy_v0.name: last-green-worker
baseline_policy_v0.rule: if a prior worker receipt says VERIFIED_SUCCESS, prefer that worker for the next compatible task

candidate_policy_v1.name: readiness-and-proof-aware
candidate_policy_v1.rule: before semantic worker routing, require current runtime exposure and non-contradictory worker-completion proof; otherwise abstain and repair the control-plane evidence path
candidate_policy_v1.reason: current read boundary exposes no usable worker runtime and existing execution evidence is failed or internally conflicted

requirements: never route to a worker whose current readiness is unavailable or unproven
never treat a verification-only green result as proof of worker completion when execution evidence conflicts
fail closed when no trustworthy ExecutionReceipt proves the required worker/provider path

result.what_it_supports: WorldLoop can apply the same route -> verify -> diagnose -> policy-change abstraction to a real changing execution fabric, including choosing not to call an agent when runtime proof is unhealthy.
result.what_it_does_not_support: This one snapshot does not prove that the candidate worker-routing policy generalizes across engineering tasks or workers. A real held-out fleet benchmark would be the next experiment.
